correctness.rationale: Words of degree at least four vanish, so scalars and cubics are central. Write the remaining parts as u in degree one and Q in degree two. If u is nonzero, a linear change of generators makes it x. On the quadratic words the kernel of [x,-] is k x^2: the three images of xy, yx and y^2 are independent by their x^2y, yx^2 and xy^2 coefficients, including in characteristic two. On linear words the degree-two component has rank one, with kernel kx, and the degree-three image of that kernel is [Q,x], already in the quadratic-input image. This gives rank four. If u=0, only the map on the two linear inputs survives. For Q nonzero it cannot vanish on both, since the quadratic centralizers of x and y intersect trivially. It has rank one precisely when it has a nonzero kernel vector l, in which case the same word calculation in a basis starting at l forces Q to be a nonzero scalar multiple of l^2. For Q with coordinates (alpha,beta,gamma,delta), this locus with its vertex included is beta=gamma and alpha delta=beta^2; on alpha nonzero take l=x+(beta/alpha)y, and when alpha=0 the equation forces beta=0 and the nonzero case is a multiple of y^2. Over the algebraic closure the resulting hypersurface is the irreducible Veronese cone; its gradient vanishes on the hypersurface only at the vertex even in characteristic two (alpha=delta=0 then forces beta=0). The tangent dimension at the vertex is three, greater than the cone dimension two. Product with the nine free central coordinates gives the stated singular locus; the rank-at-most-two locus is the linear subspace u=0 of dimension thirteen. Over F_q the punctured cone has (q+1)(q-1) points, and the remaining quadratic coefficients and free central coordinates give the four indicated multiplicities. Weighting those multiplicities by q^(-r) and dividing by q^15 gives 2q^(-4)+q^(-5)-q^(-6)-q^(-7), the stated probability.
residual_risks: Replay with python verify.py; the verifier covers four prime fields and has no scheme-theoretic or all-fields certificate.

evidence: The first comparison proves over any field that Q is rank one exactly when Q is a nonzero scalar square of a linear word. In coordinates the reduced closure is the standard cone beta=gamma, alpha delta=beta^2, which is singular at the vertex only even in characteristic two. The second comparison yields the histogram by specializing d=2 and multiplying its element counts by q. The generic centralizer sum turns either histogram into the probability.

evidence: For the radical J and normalized unit group 1+J, commutation of 1+u and 1+v is equivalent to uv=vu. Thus the class size of 1+u is the index of the linear kernel and equals q^rank ad_u. The scalar part of the unital algebra does not affect the rank, and multiplies each radical element count by q.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed Adjoint-rank gap and Veronese centralizer stratum in a truncated free algebra proves the identical characteristic-uniform ranks and counts for the identical algebra and probability. Its word argument explicitly identifies the rank-one stratum with the nonzero scalar squares over any field, not just a set of finite-field cardinalities. Adjoining the zero quadratic and free central coordinates gives the same reduced Veronese cone; its singular vertex is an immediate geometric consequence. A second indexed result for free class-three algebra groups gives the numerical part by specialization to two generators. These are exact coverage findings, not historical assertions: both indexed comparators carry later displayed dates than the frozen record. No precedence, derivation or authorship conclusion is made.
residual_risks: The relationship between these versions is unknown; later displayed record dates are not evidence of earlier publication. Existence of these exact matches settles coverage, not historical priority.

value.rationale: The rank stratification is a natural invariant of the first two-generator truncation with both quadratic and cubic commutators. But the exact census is already matched, and the probability is a weighted sum of that census. The additional dimensions and vertex calculation are routine consequences of the already identified reduced scalar-square cone and the central coordinates. The frozen statement supplies no distinct invariant or geometric refinement beyond those covered facts.
residual_risks: This is not a judgment about the value of a scheme-theoretic or higher-truncation result, neither of which is claimed.
